roundResponse.independentAssessment: The exact second circled case says the driving spindle has a positioning protruding on the bottom, followed immediately by the positioning protrusion has the same taper and then the positioning protrusion has a height. The introduced spindle entity is the sole positioning projection in this case; neither the first circled wedge-shaped projections nor the rivet-head positioning structure competes for these two immediately following spindle-projection predicates. The malformed participial spelling does not create a second introduced object. Retain the literal head positioning protruding and both existing reference edges; no textual repair or inferred structure is needed.

The same second circled case starts when the positioning structure is cone-shaped groove. It then compares the projection taper with the positioning grooves and projection height with the depth of the positioning groove. This paired taper/depth description uses the sole groove identified in that case. Case1 names notches, not grooves; claim11 names positioning surfaces but introduces no competing groove. The local plural/singular variation therefore does not leave two plausible groove introductions. Existing references to cone-shaped groove remain justified while all source number/spelling variation is preserved.

Following of the driving spindle fixes component ownership. The ancestor positioning structure belongs to the rivet head, so withholding a spindle-side antecedent is determinate rather than uncertain.

The following on the top of the rivet head fixes these as the head-side rotary driving structures introduced in11. The earlier rotary driving structures on the bottom of the driving spindle are a different component-side referent and remain unlinked.
Of the driving spindle fixes the same spindle lower surface introduced in11.c. Bottom/lower is a directional alias with the same explicit component owner, so its current edge is justified.

Step1 expressly applies appropriate resistance to restrain rivet motion; the Step3 force condition exceeds the resistance applied to that rivet. No alternative applied resistance is introduced. The existing edge is justified by the process grammar.
